turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
Before we start? We started on November 3rd, when the zero went into the gradebook. You reread them this morning, a week after you'd already decided, so what exactly did they tell you?
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. If my son writes that well, then you've just made my point for me. Is there a document, or are you going to compliment your way through this?
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.

Then why are we here? A thoughtful kid with a zero he found out about in front of his class. I'm writing down that you said "I mean that," and in about twenty minutes I'm taking this to the principal.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
It became a fight when you entered the zero before you picked up the phone. Caring doesn't go in the gradebook, Hale. Withdraw the zero, or show me what you based it on.
